examples.ko: 도로 옆 가드레일이 부서져서 수리하고 있어요.
examples.en: The guardrail beside the road is broken, so they're repairing it.

examples.ko: 차가 가드레일을 들이받았지만 다행히 다친 사람은 없어요.
examples.en: A car hit the guardrail, but fortunately no one was hurt.

examples.ko: 산길 가드레일 덕분에 낭떠러지로 떨어지지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the guardrail on the mountain road, we didn't fall off the cliff.

examples.ko: 가드레일에 부딪힌 차가 길가에 서 있어요.
examples.en: A car that hit the guardrail is stopped at the roadside.

examples.ko: 새로 생긴 가드레일은 눈에 잘 띄는 색이에요.
examples.en: The new guardrail is a color that stands out well.
I could see the sea beyond the highway guardrail.

explain: 도로 옆이나 낭떠러지 쪽에 차가 벗어나지 않게 세운 철제 안전 울타리예요. 다리, 계단, 발코니의 손잡이는 보통 '난간'이라고 불러서 구별해요. 교통사고 뉴스에서 '가드레일을 들이받다'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The car slid on the snowy road and hit the guardrail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들이받다'보다 중립적인 사고 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more neutral way to describe a crash than '들이받다'.

phrases.en: They installed a guardrail on the dangerous road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 공사 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about safety work.

phrases.en: They are repairing the broken guardrail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망가진 가드레일을 고친다는 뜻으로, 도로 공사 소식에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means fixing a damaged guardrail; common in road-work news.

explain_en: It is the metal safety barrier set beside roads or cliff edges to keep cars from leaving the road. The rails on bridges, stairs and balconies are usually called '난간', which keeps the two apart. It often appears in traffic accident news as '가드레일을 들이받다' (to crash into the guardrail).

examples.en: Farmers harvest the rice in autumn.

examples.ko: 올해는 날씨가 좋아서 사과를 많이 거두어들일 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The weather was good this year, so we could harvest a lot of apples.
The government withdrew the plan it announced last month.

examples.ko: 콩을 거두어들이려면 비가 오기 전에 서둘러야 해요.
examples.en: To harvest the beans, you have to hurry before it rains.

examples.ko: 나라가 세금을 거두어들이는 방법은 여러 가지예요.
examples.en: There are several ways a country collects taxes.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 한 말이지만 이제 거두어들이고 싶어요.
examples.en: I said it in anger, but now I want to take it back.

explain: 곡식을 수확하는 것 외에 성과나 세금을 얻거나, 했던 말이나 결정을 없던 일로 하는 뜻으로도 써요. '거둬들이다'는 이 말을 줄인 모양이에요. 성과에는 '성과를 거두다'라고 짧게 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: In autumn, farmers bring in the rice harvest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거두어들이다'를 줄인 말로 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 거두어들이다, more casual in conversation.

phrases.en: Farmers harvest apples.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식이나 과일을 거둘 때 쓰는 더 쉽고 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more common word for harvesting crops or fruit.

phrases.en: I studied hard and got good results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력해서 좋은 결과를 얻었다는 뜻으로 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to say you got good results through effort.

explain_en: Besides harvesting crops, it is used for gaining results or taxes, and for taking back words or decisions. '거둬들이다' is the contracted form of this word. For results, people also say the shorter '성과를 거두다'.

en: to be constructed; to be built

examples.en: The new system will be set up within this year.

examples.ko: 서로 믿는 관계가 구축되기까지 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time before a relationship of trust is built.
A Wi-Fi network was set up at the school.
Once the data is built up, searching gets easy.
We inspected the facilities that had been set up.
A secure security system is being built.

explain: 눈에 보이는 건물보다 시스템·네트워크·관계·데이터처럼 틀을 차근차근 쌓아서 만든다는 뜻이에요. 건물을 짓는 일에는 '건설되다', '짓다'를 써요. 뉴스와 회사 문서에서 자주 나오고, 능동은 '구축하다'예요.

phrases.en: The company builds a new network.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구축되다'의 능동형으로, 만드는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form; the builder is the subject.

phrases.en: Building the system takes two months.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구축'은 회사나 뉴스에서 명사로도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 구축 is often used in business and news.

phrases.en: The database has already been built.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 만들어진 상태가 지금도 이어지고 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses that it was built and the result still stands.

explain_en: Rather than physical buildings, it fits frameworks built up step by step: systems, networks, relationships and data. For buildings use 건설되다 or 짓다. It is frequent in news and company documents; the active is 구축하다.

examples.en: The film received high praise from critics.
I felt great about the teacher's glowing praise.
Rave reviews poured in for this restaurant.
The boss's lavish praise gave me energy.
The new product earned rave reviews right after its launch.
The high praise is nice, but it's also pressure.

explain: '칭찬'보다 훨씬 강하게 최고라고 말하는 것이에요. 보통 '극찬을 받다', '극찬이 쏟아지다'로 쓰고, 뉴스나 리뷰에서 많이 나와요. 평범한 칭찬에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Great praise poured in for the new movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬이 한꺼번에 많이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a lot of praise comes out all at once.

phrases.example: 평론가들이 이 책에 극찬을 아끼지 않았어요.
phrases.en: Critics did not hold back their high praise for this book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 크게 칭찬했다는 뜻으로 리뷰에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means they praised greatly; common in reviews.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 새 노래로 극찬을 받았어요.
phrases.en: The singer received high praise for the new song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 칭찬받았을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for being praised greatly.

explain_en: This is far stronger than 칭찬: it says something is the best. The usual patterns are 극찬을 받다 and 극찬이 쏟아지다, common in news and reviews. It isn't used for ordinary compliments.

en: so very; really really; way too

examples.en: The movie I watched yesterday was so, so fun.
I missed you so much. Have you been well?

examples.ko: 오늘은 너무너무 피곤해서 일찍 잘 거예요.
examples.en: I'm so, so tired today, so I'll sleep early.
Thank you, I'm so, so grateful!
The child was overjoyed to get the present.

examples.ko: 이 떡볶이는 너무너무 매워서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This tteokbokki is so very spicy that it is hard to eat.

explain: '너무'를 반복해서 감정을 더 강하게 말하는 구어체예요. 원래 '너무'는 정도가 지나친 것을 뜻했지만 지금은 좋은 뜻에도 '너무 좋아요'처럼 흔히 써요. 글보다 말에서, 특히 친한 사이에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The weather is so nice today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 짧고 평소에 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and the most common everyday form.

phrases.en: Thank you so, so much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 강조하는 말이고 기분 좋은 말에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar emphatic repetition, often for happy feelings.

phrases.en: I really, really like this song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 감정을 아주 강하게 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for expressing strong positive feelings.

explain_en: A spoken, emphatic repeat of '너무'. '너무' originally meant 'too much' but is now routinely used for good things too, like '너무 좋아요'. It is more of a spoken, friendly form than written.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 외딴곳에 작은 집을 짓고 살아요.
examples.en: That couple built a small house in a secluded place and live there.
It's a remote place, so it's very quiet at night.
I walked all the way to a remote place where phones get no signal.
Even though the restaurant is in a remote spot, it has a lot of customers.
I got lost and spent a night in an isolated place.
Wouldn't it be inconvenient to move to a secluded place?

explain: '외딴섬', '외딴집'처럼 '외딴'은 뒤에 장소를 붙여 써요. 쓸쓸하고 다른 곳과 떨어진 느낌이 있어서 '시골'과는 달라요. 시골은 도시가 아닌 지역이고, 외딴곳은 주변과 떨어진 곳이에요.

phrases.example: 산 아래에 외딴집이 한 채 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a lone house at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 집과 멀리 떨어진 집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A house standing far from other houses.

phrases.en: That singer lives on a remote island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 육지나 다른 섬과 떨어진 섬을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An island far from the mainland or other islands.

phrases.en: That grandfather lives in a secluded place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많지 않은 멀리 떨어진 곳에 산다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means living in a faraway place with few people around.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a secluded place

explain_en: '외딴' attaches to a place noun, as in '외딴섬' and '외딴집'. It has a lonely, cut-off feeling, so it differs from '시골' (countryside), which just means a non-urban area. '외딴곳' stresses being apart from its surroundings.

examples.en: You need willpower to go on a diet.
You can build willpower through practice.
He passed the exam through strong willpower.
There are times when willpower alone is not enough to hold out.

examples.ko: 의지력을 기르려고 매일 아침 일찍 일어나요.
examples.en: I get up early every morning to build willpower.
People with willpower see things through to the end.

explain: '의지력이 강하다/약하다'로 자주 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '끈기'가 있는데, 끈기는 포기하지 않고 계속하는 힘이고 의지력은 마음먹은 것을 해내려는 힘이에요. 그냥 '의지'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 의지력이 강해서 끝까지 해요.
phrases.en: He has strong willpower, so he finishes things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음먹은 것을 해내는 힘이 크다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means having great strength to carry out what you set your mind to.

phrases.example: 저는 의지력이 약해서 자꾸 간식을 먹어요.
phrases.en: My willpower is weak, so I keep eating snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강하다'의 반대로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '강하다'.

phrases.en: You need willpower to keep exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-력' 없이 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter form without '-력'.

explain_en: You often say '의지력이 강하다/약하다'. A similar word is '끈기', which is the staying power to keep going, while 의지력 is the strength of will to do what you decided. People also just say '의지'.

examples.en: There aren't many transport options to that island.
If you arrive late at night, there's no way to get back.

examples.ko: 차편을 미리 알아보고 출발하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to check transport options before you set out.

examples.ko: 시골이라 읍내까지 가는 차편이 하루에 두 번뿐이에요.
examples.en: It's the countryside, so there are only two rides a day to town.

examples.ko: 친구가 차편을 마련해 줘서 편하게 왔어요.
examples.en: A friend arranged a ride for me, so I got here comfortably.

examples.ko: 공연장까지 가는 차편 좀 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to get to the concert hall.

explain: 버스, 기차, 택시처럼 어디로 갈 때 이용할 수 있는 교통수단을 말해요. '있다, 없다, 알아보다, 마련하다'와 잘 어울려요. 같은 뜻으로 '교통편'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The transportation is convenient, so I go often.
phrases.nuance_ko: '차편'과 같은 뜻이고, 버스와 기차 외에도 넓게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as '차편' and can be used broadly beyond buses and trains.

phrases.en: I looked into transportation before the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈 방법을 미리 찾아볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for checking ahead on how to get somewhere.

phrases.en: I arranged transportation to get to the venue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈 방법을 준비해 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when preparing a way to get somewhere.

explain_en: It refers to the transportation you can use to get somewhere, such as a bus, train or taxi. It pairs well with '있다', '없다', '알아보다' and '마련하다'. '교통편' is also widely used with the same meaning.

examples.en: Does reading mystery novels improve your reasoning skills too?

examples.ko: 추리력을 키우려고 퍼즐 게임을 자주 해요.
examples.en: I play puzzle games often to build up my reasoning skills.
Is reasoning ability something you're born with?
It's a quiz that needs both reasoning and observation skills.

examples.ko: 추리력 때문에 친구들이 저를 탐정이라고 불러요.
examples.en: Because of my reasoning skills, my friends call me a detective.

examples.ko: 추리력이 뛰어난 사람은 작은 단서도 놓치지 않아요.
examples.en: People with great reasoning ability don't miss even small clues.

explain: 단서를 모아서 답을 알아내는 힘이에요. '관찰력', '판단력', '이해력'처럼 '-력'이 붙은 말과 같이 알아 두세요. 사람 마음을 알아채는 '눈치'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: That detective has excellent reasoning ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이 좋다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's ability.

phrases.en: Puzzles are good for building reasoning skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력을 키울 때 '기르다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '기르다' is often used for developing an ability.

phrases.en: This game requires reasoning skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이나 게임에 필요한 능력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what skill a task or game needs.

explain_en: It's the ability to gather clues and work out the answer. Learn it together with other '-력' words like '관찰력', '판단력' and '이해력'. It's different from '눈치', which is about sensing what people feel.

examples.en: Living alone in a foreign country is lonely.
He wandered through foreign lands for a long time.
The culture of another country feels strange at first.
Life in a foreign land was not easy.
When I go abroad, I miss my hometown's food.
I have a friend who married someone from another country.

explain: '외국'은 우리나라 밖의 나라를 두루 말하고, '타국'은 '남의 나라'라는 느낌이 있어서 고향을 떠난 쓸쓸함이나 오랜 타향살이 이야기에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '외국'을 훨씬 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Even though life in a foreign land was hard, I endured.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고향을 떠나 사는 외로운 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a lonely feeling of living away from home.

phrases.en: I spent Lunar New Year in a foreign land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '땅'을 붙이면 글 같은 쓸쓸한 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'ttang' gives a more literary, lonely tone.

phrases.en: I work in a foreign country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '타국'보다 '외국'을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, 'oegug' is used far more than 'tagug'.

explain_en: 외국 is the everyday word for any country outside your own, while 타국 means 'someone else's country' and fits stories of homesickness or long life away. In daily conversation 외국 is much more common.

examples.en: I put a table clock on my desk.
I woke up to the table clock's alarm.
I got a table clock as a birthday present.
The table clock is five minutes slow.
After I changed the battery, the table clock works again.
A quiet table clock is good for a bedroom.

explain: 책상이나 탁자 위에 놓고 쓰는 작은 시계예요. 벽에 거는 '벽시계', 손목에 차는 '손목시계'와 짝으로 기억해 두세요. 알람이 있으면 '알람시계'나 '자명종'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: I set my alarm clock to get up early tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알람 기능이 있는 시계를 말하고, 탁상시계일 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clock with an alarm; often a table clock.

phrases.en: The alarm clock rang and I woke up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '알람시계'와 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 옛날 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '알람시계' but sounds a bit old-fashioned.

phrases.en: I put a table clock next to my bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁상시계를 어디에 두었는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you placed the clock.

explain_en: It is a small clock placed on a desk or table. Remember it alongside '벽시계' (wall clock) and '손목시계' (wristwatch). With an alarm it may also be called '알람시계' or '자명종'.

examples.ko: 요즘은 회갑보다 칠순이나 팔순에 잔치를 하는 집이 많아요.
examples.en: These days, more families hold a party for the 70th or 80th birthday than the 60th.
We held Grandfather's 80th birthday party at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 다음 달이 어머니 팔순이라서 선물을 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: Next month is my mother's 80th birthday, so I'm thinking about a gift.
We gave flowers to our teacher, who turned eighty.
Even though she is over eighty, she is really vigorous.

examples.ko: 가족이 모여 팔순 기념 여행을 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: The family got together and took a trip for the 80th birthday.

explain: 여든 살 또는 여든 번째 해를 가리키는 말이라서 보통 어르신의 생신을 말할 때 써요. '환갑(회갑), 칠순, 팔순, 구순'처럼 나이마다 잔치 이름이 있어요. 높임말로 '팔순을 맞으시다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 외할머니 팔순 잔치가 있어요.
phrases.en: My maternal grandmother's 80th birthday party is next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여든 살 생신을 축하하는 잔치예요. 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A party celebrating an 80th birthday. The most common collocation.

phrases.en: My grandmother turned eighty this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신께 쓰는 높임 표현이에요. 윗사람 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful expression for elders, used when talking about someone senior.

phrases.en: My father will turn eighty next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되다'에 높임을 붙인 말이에요. 미래의 일에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form of '되다'. It can also be used for future events.

explain_en: It refers to age eighty and is used for an elder's birthday. Koreans have names for milestone celebrations: '환갑(회갑), 칠순, 팔순, 구순'. For honorific speech, say '팔순을 맞으시다'.
